title: Tara's arrival at Vali in battlefield
introduction: Lady Tara rushes out to reach her slain husband while the monkey generals seek of her to anoint Angada as king immediately or leave Kishkindha, for Sugreeva and his men may come occupying the city. She chides their advises away and proceeds to meet Vali. She arrives at that place, sees Rama and his brother Lakshmana, her husband Vali and his brother Sugreeva. She faints and wails for the departing soul of Vali.
closing: इति वाल्मीकि रामायणे आदि काव्ये किष्किन्ध काण्डे एकोनविंशः सर्गः
Thus, this is the 19th chapter in Kishkindha Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic poem of India.

verses.devanagari:
स वानर महाराजः शयानः शर पीडितः |
प्रत्युक्तो हेतुमद् वाक्यैः न उत्तरम् प्रत्यपद्यत
verses.iast:
sa vānara mahārājaḥ śayānaḥ śara pīḍitaḥ |
pratyukto hetumad vākyaiḥ na uttaram pratyapadyata
verses.translation: That great vanara king Vali who is sprawling agonised by arrow, and to whom Rama gave a reply with well-reasoned words did not find any other reply to be given to Rama.

glosses.meaning: in return, who is said [replied by Rama]
not, in turn, he derived, - find another reply.

verses.devanagari:
अश्मभिः परिभिन्न अंगः पादपैर् आहतो भृशम् |
राम बाणेन च आक्रान्तो जीवित अंते मुमोह सः
verses.iast:
aśmabhiḥ paribhinna aṃgaḥ pādapair āhato bhṛśam |
rāma bāṇena ca ākrānto jīvita aṃte mumoha saḥ
verses.translation: He who is heavily thrashed with trees, whose limbs are variously cracked with boulders, and whom Rama's arrow finally vanquished, that Vali fainted at the time of his breathing his last.

glosses.meaning: with boulders, variously, cracked, with limbs
he, at life, ending - at the time of breathing last, fainted.

verses.devanagari:
तम् भार्या बाण मोक्षेण राम दत्तेन संयुगे |
हतम् प्लवग शार्दूलम् तारा शुश्राव वालिनम्
verses.iast:
tam bhāryā bāṇa mokṣeṇa rāma dattena saṃyuge |
hatam plavaga śārdūlam tārā śuśrāva vālinam
verses.translation: Tara, wife of Vali, heard that the tigerly monkey Vali perished in fight by the arrow released by Rama.
notes: This is also said as 'by the salvation accorded by Rama through his arrow...' rāma datten śara mokśeṇa, but it is said to be a squeezed meaning according to the style of old Sanskrit.

verses.devanagari:
सा सपुत्र अप्रियम् श्रुत्वा वधम् भर्तुः सुदारुणम् |
निष्पपात भृशम् तस्मात् उद्विग्ना गिरि कंदरात्
verses.iast:
sā saputra apriyam śrutvā vadham bhartuḥ sudāruṇam |
niṣpapāta bhṛśam tasmāt udvignā giri kaṃdarāt
verses.translation: On hearing the very gruesome killing of her husband that is unpleasant, she is highly anguished and rushed out of Kishkindha along with Angada.

glosses.meaning: from, that mountain's, cave - say Kishkindha

verses.devanagari:
ये ते अंगद परीवारा वानरा हि महाबलाः |
ते सकार्मुकम् आलोक्य रामम् त्रस्ताः प्रदुद्रुवुः
verses.iast:
ye te aṃgada parīvārā vānarā hi mahābalāḥ |
te sakārmukam ālokya rāmam trastāḥ pradudruvuḥ
verses.translation: On seeing Rama with bow those very mighty vanara-s that form the escort of Angada are scared to death, and they very quickly fled from there towards Kishkindha.

glosses.meaning: those, very mighty vanara-s are there

verses.devanagari:
सा ददर्श ततः त्रस्तान् हरीन् आपततो द्रुतम् |
यूथाद् इव परिभ्रष्टान् मृगान् निहत यूथपान्
verses.iast:
sā dadarśa tataḥ trastān harīn āpatato drutam |
yūthād iva paribhraṣṭān mṛgān nihata yūthapān
verses.translation: Then on her way towards field of combat she saw the monkeys that are frightened and fleeing in disorder, like those animals that have wandered off from their herd when their master is killed.

glosses.meaning: that have killed, troop leader - master

verses.devanagari:
तान् उवाच समासाद्य दुःखितान् दुःखिता सती |
राम वित्रासितान् सर्वान् अनुबद्धान् इव इषुभिः
verses.iast:
tān uvāca samāsādya duḥkhitān duḥkhitā satī |
rāma vitrāsitān sarvān anubaddhān iva iṣubhiḥ
verses.translation: Nearing those monkeys that are already distressed at the fall of Vali, and that are highly frightened by Rama, and that are fleeing as though Rama's arrow is still tracking them down, Tara spoke to all of them, distressed as she is.

glosses.meaning: by arrows, followed closely - tracked down, as though

verses.devanagari:
वानरा राज सिंहस्य यस्य यूयम् पुरः सराः |
तम् विहाय सुवित्रस्ताः कस्माद् द्रवत दुर्गताः
verses.iast:
vānarā rāja siṃhasya yasya yūyam puraḥ sarāḥ |
tam vihāya suvitrastāḥ kasmād dravata durgatāḥ
verses.translation: "Oh! Vanara-s, what for you are running away in utter fright and desperation, leaving off your best king to whom all of you are ushers?" Thus Tara enquired with the monkeys.

verses.devanagari:
राज्य हेतोः स चेत् भ्राता भ्रात्रा कॄरेण पातितः |
रामेण प्रसृतैः दूरात् मार्गणैः दूर पातिभिः
verses.iast:
rājya hetoḥ sa cet bhrātā bhrātrā kṝreṇa pātitaḥ |
rāmeṇa prasṛtaiḥ dūrāt mārgaṇaiḥ dūra pātibhiḥ
verses.translation: "Whether or not a cruel brother made his brother to fall for the reason of kingdom with the arrows of Rama which can surge well from distance and fall on distant target? Aver it.
notes: There is a grammarian's problem in this verse. The word cet usually used for ' if...' Then the meaning obtained is "If a brother is felled by his brother for the sake of kingdom, what if and why do you fear?" Then this may not justify Tara's decency. And if this cet is taken as praśnārthaka 'interrogative...' then it may mean that she is trying to ascertain whether Vali is dead or still alive, to have a last glimpse. And enquiring in anguish would be normal in such situations. It may be correct to use 'whether' because it ensues 'not' and also as an alternative interrogative. And 'if' is used it is 'if of ignorance' but not 'of certainty' or 'of chance'. Anyway she is interested in information and orderliness of monkeys.

verses.devanagari:
कपि पत्न्या वचः श्रुत्वा कपयः काम रूपिणः |
प्राप्त कालम् अविश्लिष्टम् ऊचुर् वचनम् अंगनाम्
verses.iast:
kapi patnyā vacaḥ śrutvā kapayaḥ kāma rūpiṇaḥ |
prāpta kālam aviśliṣṭam ūcur vacanam aṃganām
verses.translation: On hearing the words of monkey's wife those guise-changing monkeys spoke this sentence coherently to lady Tara, befitting to present time of chaos.

verses.devanagari:
जीवपुत्रे निवर्तस्व पुत्रम् रक्षस्व च अन्दगम् |
अंतको राम रूपेण हत्वा नयति वालिनम्
verses.iast:
jīvaputre nivartasva putram rakṣasva ca andagam |
aṃtako rāma rūpeṇa hatvā nayati vālinam
verses.translation: "Return, oh, lady with a living son, and safeguard Angada, for the Terminator in the form of Rama is taking away Vali on killing.

glosses.meaning: alive, son - oh, one with a living son
Vali, on killing, leading away - taking away.

verses.devanagari:
क्षिप्तान् वृक्षान् समाविध्य विपुलाः च शिलाः तथा |
वाली वज्र समैर् बाणैर् वज्रेण इव निपातितः
verses.iast:
kṣiptān vṛkṣān samāvidhya vipulāḥ ca śilāḥ tathā |
vālī vajra samair bāṇair vajreṇa iva nipātitaḥ
verses.translation: "Shattering trees and massive boulders that Vali hurled at him with thunderbolt like arrows Rama felled Vali as if by thunderbolt.
notes: The plural number given to the 'arrows' may be observed. Rama shot Vali with only one arrow but each monkey is multiplying one arrow to become many. Rumours multiply thus.

verses.devanagari:
अभिभूतम् इदम् सर्वम् विद्रुतम् वानरम् बलम् |
अस्मिन् प्लवग शार्दूले हते शक्र सम प्रभे
verses.iast:
abhibhūtam idam sarvam vidrutam vānaram balam |
asmin plavaga śārdūle hate śakra sama prabhe
verses.translation: "When that tigerly fly-jumper Vali whose brilliance is similar to Indra is killed all this vanara force felt defenceless and fled.

verses.devanagari:
रक्ष्यताम् नगरम् शूरैर् अंगदः च अभिषिच्यताम् |
पदस्थम् वालिनः पुत्रम् भजिष्यन्ति प्लवंगमाः
verses.iast:
rakṣyatām nagaram śūrair aṃgadaḥ ca abhiṣicyatām |
padastham vālinaḥ putram bhajiṣyanti plavaṅgamāḥ
verses.translation: "Let the city of Kishkindha be safeguarded and let Angada be anointed, and when Vali's son Angada is enthroned all the fly-jumpers will stand by him.

glosses.meaning: city, by brave ones, be safeguarded

verses.devanagari:
अथवा अरुचितम् स्थानम् इह ते रुचिरानने |
आविशन्ति हि दुर्गाणि क्षिप्रम् अद्य एव वानराः
verses.iast:
athavā arucitam sthānam iha te rucirānane |
āviśanti hi durgāṇi kṣipram adya eva vānarāḥ
verses.translation: "Or, your staying here is not good, oh, one with a pleasant visage, for those monkeys of Sugreeva will promptly enter our strongholds on this day itself.

glosses.meaning: oh, one with pleasant, face Tara

verses.devanagari:
अभार्याः सह भार्याः च सन्ति अत्र वन चारिणः |
लुब्धेभ्यो विप्रलब्धेयः तेभ्यो नः सुमहद् भयम्
verses.iast:
abhāryāḥ saha bhāryāḥ ca santi atra vana cāriṇaḥ |
lubdhebhyo vipralabdheyaḥ tebhyo naḥ sumahad bhayam
verses.translation: "There are foresters in Kishkindha, some with wives and some without, some hankering after wives, some whom we have victimised, and from them we have very great danger." So said monkeys to Tara.
notes: Even in capital many followed the suite of Vali in incarcerating other's wives. Now they all may turn up since Sugreeva won the battle, assaulting such followers of Vali's style of living. This is the fear of individuals reported to Tara.

glosses.meaning: forest, moving ones, in there [in Kishkindha,] are there
those that are victimised by us

verses.devanagari:
अल्पांतर गतानाम् तु श्रुत्वा वचनम् अंगना |
आत्मनः प्रतिरूपम् सा बभाषे चारु हासिनी
verses.iast:
alpāṃtara gatānām tu śrutvā vacanam aṃganā |
ātmanaḥ pratirūpam sā babhāṣe cāru hāsinī
verses.translation: On going a small distance ahead after listening those words, she whose smile will be winsome, that lady Tara said this befitting to her personality.
notes: The word apla antara is usually 'a little after...' But Prof. Satya Vrat includes this under rare words/expressions of Ramayana and gives meaning as 'small distance...' In any way a pause occurs now for her to reply. She is going towards the place where Vali is and monkeys are following her. She paced still ahead, gained a pause and then started to speak to them.

verses.devanagari:
पुत्रेण मम किम् कार्यम् किम् राज्येन किम् आत्मना |
कपि सिम्हे महा भागे तस्मिन् भर्तरि नश्यति
verses.iast:
putreṇa mama kim kāryam kim rājyena kim ātmanā |
kapi simhe mahā bhāge tasmin bhartari naśyati
verses.translation: "Of what avail is a son, or a kingdom, or I to myself when my husband that lion like monkey with great honour perished.

verses.devanagari:
पाद मूलम् गमिष्यामि तस्य एव अहम् महात्मनः |
यो असौ राम प्रयुक्तेन शरेण विनिपातितः
verses.iast:
pāda mūlam gamiṣyāmi tasya eva aham mahātmanaḥ |
yo asau rāma prayuk{}tena śareṇa vinipātitaḥ
verses.translation: "I wish to consign myself at the base of foot of that great-soul, who is felled down by the arrow projected by Rama." So said Tara to fleeing monkeys.

glosses.meaning: I, wish to go - I consign myself [on pyre.]

verses.devanagari:
एवम् उक्त्वा प्रदुद्राव रुदती शोक मूर्च्छिता |
शिरः च उरः च बाहुभ्याम् दुःखेन समभिघ्नती
verses.iast:
evam uk{}tvā pradudrāva rudatī śoka mūrcchitā |
śiraḥ ca uraḥ ca bāhubhyām duḥkhena samabhighnatī
verses.translation: Saying thus she started to wail and convulse in agony, and slapped her head and chest with both of her hands while she speedily rushed towards Vali.

verses.devanagari:
सा व्रजन्ती ददर्श अथ पतिम् निपतितम् भुवि |
हन्तारम् दानव इन्द्राणाम् समरेषु अनिवर्तिनाम्
verses.iast:
sā vrajantī dadarśa atha patim nipatitam bhuvi |
hantāram dānava indrāṇām samareṣu anivartinām
verses.translation: While she is still trudging then she saw her husband who is the destroyer of arch-demons like Maayaavi and Dundubhi, and who never retreated in combats, but now fallen down on ground.

glosses.meaning: in combats, back, coming - not, retreating

verses.devanagari:
क्षेप्तारम् पर्वत इन्द्राणाम् वज्राणाम् इव वासवम् |
महावात समाविष्टम् महामेघ औघ निःस्वनम्
verses.iast:
kṣeptāram parvata indrāṇām vajrāṇām iva vāsavam |
mahāvāta samāviṣṭam mahāmegha augha niḥsvanam
verses.translation: She saw Vali who is a flinger of loftiest mountains as with Indra flinging his thunderbolt, who is a blaster as with great gusty winds, and who is a roarer as with a cluster of great black-clouds.

glosses.meaning: mountains, the lofty ones, flinger of
great, gust of winds, similar, having blast

verses.devanagari:
शक्रतुल्य पराक्रांतम् वृष्ट्वा इव उपरतम् घनम् |
नर्दन्तम् नर्दताम् भीमम् शूरम् शूरेण पातितम् |
शार्दूलेन आमिषस्य अर्थे मृग राजम् इव आहतम्
verses.iast:
śakratulya parākrāṃtam vṛṣṭvā iva uparatam ghanam |
nardantam nardatām bhīmam śūram śūreṇa pātitam |
śārdūlena āmiṣasya arthe mṛga rājam iva āhatam
verses.translation: He who equals Indra in the invasion of enemies, a violent thunderer at the opponent thunderers, a brave one felled by still brave one, and who is like a best animal killed by a tiger for the purpose of flesh, and quietened like black-cloud at the end of downpour, At him she saw.
notes: Some commentators negate this simile of tiger to Rama, saying it abhuuta upama 'impossible smile...' By virtue Rama himself is the lion-king and comparing him with a lesser animal like tiger is objected, though Rama did not eliminate Vali for flesh or meat. The word shaarduula textually means a tiger in the present day context. For this commentators bring in the rulebook vyjayanti which says shaarduula also means a lion -siñho mṛga indraḥ pañcāsyo haryakṣaḥ śveta piñgalaḥ vyādīrnāsyo mahānādaḥ śārdūlo amita vikrama

glosses.meaning: for flesh, for the purpose of

verses.devanagari:
अर्चितम् सर्व लोकस्य सपताकम् सवेदिकम् |
नाग हेतोः सुपर्णेन चैत्यम् उन्मथितम् यथा
verses.iast:
arcitam sarva lokasya sapatākam savedikam |
nāga hetoḥ suparṇena caityam unmathitam yathā
verses.translation: He who is like a sanctum that is hitherto worshipped by all people, that is decorated with flags and demarcated with podia, but just ravaged by an eagle for the sake of a snake which sneaked into that sanctum, and Tara saw such a Vali plumped on the ground.
notes: The word caitya is not to be confounded with Buddhist monastery. In villages, even today, people will prepare a makeshift sanctum adorning it with a podium and flags for worships, and that being an open place snakes sneak in, for which eagles will come and sit on the flagstaff, and when catching its prey that eagle kicks off the flag post, and by the fall of that flagstaff that makeshift sanctum gets plumped onto ground.

glosses.meaning: snake, for the reason of, [as with]

verses.devanagari:
अवष्टभ्य अवतिष्ठंतम् ददर्श धनुर् ऊर्जितम् |
रामम् रामानुजम् चैव भर्तुः चैव तथा अनुजम्
verses.iast:
avaṣṭabhya avatiṣṭhaṃtam dadarśa dhanur ūrjitam |
rāmam rāmānujam caiva bhartuḥ caiva tathā anujam
verses.translation: She saw Rama standing and abutting on his very powerful bow, and his younger brother Lakshmana, even at the younger brother of her husband, namely Sugreeva.
notes: This verse reminds us of the results from brotherly love-hate, younger-elder brother relation. Lakshmana is appearing behind Rama while Sugreeva, over dying Vali.

glosses.meaning: at Rama, Rama's, younger brother - Lakshmana, also thus
husband's, younger brother - Sugreeva, also thus

verses.devanagari:
तान् अतीत्य समासाद्य भर्तारम् निहतम् रणे |
समीक्ष्य व्यथिता भूमौ संभ्रांता निपपात ह
verses.iast:
tān atītya samāsādya bhartāram nihatam raṇe |
samīkṣya vyathitā bhūmau sambhrāṃtā nipapāta ha
verses.translation: Going past them she reached her husband who is routed in combat, and on observing him closely she indeed fell down on earth as she is distraught and dumbfounded.

verses.devanagari:
सुप्ता इव पुनर् उत्थाय आर्य पुत्र इति वादिनी |
रुरोद सा पतिम् दृष्ट्वा सम्वीतम् मृत्यु दामभिः
verses.iast:
suptā iva punar utthāya ārya putra iti vādinī |
ruroda sā patim dṛṣṭvā samvītam mṛtyu dāmabhiḥ
verses.translation: On getting up as though reawakened from sleep she saw her husband bound fast by the strings of death, and then she wailingly addressed him as, "oh, nobleman's son..."

verses.devanagari:
ताम् अवेक्ष्य तु सुग्रीवः क्रोशन्तीम् कुररीम् इव |
विषादम् अगमत् कष्टम् दृष्ट्वा च अंगदम् आगतम्
verses.iast:
tām avekṣya tu sugrīvaḥ krośantīm kurarīm iva |
viṣādam agamat kaṣṭam dṛṣṭvā ca aṃgadam āgatam
verses.translation: On observing her who is wailing like a female osprey, and even on looking at Angada who arrived there, a miserable remorse came upon Sugreeva.

glosses.meaning: one who arrived, Angada, also, on seeing
